page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance designed for computational workloads requiring dedicated CPU performance. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, the server is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. It provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-CPU ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM allocated per core.

Networking and peripheral specifications include a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, facilitating consistent throughput for standard distributed operations. The instance does not include integrated local storage, meaning primary disk operations rely on external block storage services. Additionally, the instance contains no GPU acceleration hardware and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent instruction execution without contention from shared hyperthreads or neighboring tenants. By prioritizing compute capacity over larger memory footprints, the instance maintains cost-effective resource utilization for CPU-bound tasks. The absence of bundled local NVMe drives represents an operational tradeoff, directing this server away from high-IOPS local storage needs in favor of decoupled, elastic storage configurations.

Workloads aligned with the ecs.c9a.2xlarge hardware profile include front-end web server fleets, build and compilation nodes within CI/CD pipelines, lightweight data processing, video encoding, and distributed batch computing tasks where core throughput outweighs large in-memory caching requirements.
